text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic was elected president of Yugoslavia on Tuesday by the federal parliament.
Milosevic moved to the new office because the Serbian constitution prevented him from seeking the Serbian presidency for a third time.
Milosevic, nominated by the ruling Serbian Socialist party (SPS) and the Montenegrin DPS was the only candidate and gained comfortable majorities in a secret ballot of both chambers of parliament.
A national election to replace him as Serbian president will be held within two months.
He will take the oath as federal president on July 23.

The federal presidency was mainly a ceremonial post under previous incumbents but Milosevic is expected to remain Yugoslavia's main power broker through his control of the SPS, police and state bureaucracy.
